title.zh: 解析分布的 Hilbert 与 Cauchy 变换
title.en: Evaluate a safe analytic expression and its derivative transforms.

summary: Evaluate a safe analytic expression and its derivative transforms.

identity.definition: DensityExpression interprets the restricted AST and propagates analytic first derivatives by chain rules without eval or SymPy. Real-axis integrands subtract f(x)*exp(-(v-x)²), whose whole-line odd PV vanishes. Boundary values add i*pi*f(x); optional lower continuation adds 2*pi*i*f(z). For |z|>=12 the vanishing-endpoint identity Zp=Cauchy[v*fprime]/z avoids cancellation of the zero-mass derivative; the absolute quadrature tolerance scales inversely with phase magnitude. The density derivative and its analytic continuation are not reconstructed from rounded Z or epsilon.
identity.direction: Declared inputs to declared scientific outputs
identity.coordinates: Dimensionless real velocity and complex phase or frequency
identity.boundary: Infinite real velocity contour with stated continuation or finite support.
assumptions: Density is real and integrable on the real contour.
No collective-mode uniqueness or certified global quadrature bound is asserted.
Expression has a valid analytic extension where continuation is requested.
Explicit increasing mesh resolves all density features and tails.

inputs.name: z
inputs.description: Complex phase point z=omega/(sqrt(2)*k) for the Maxwellian normalization.

inputs.name: expression
inputs.description: Analytic density in v using finite real constants, pi, arithmetic and exp/log/sqrt/sin/cos/sinh/cosh/tanh; MATLAB point operators accepted.
inputs.constraints: Real integrable density with decaying derivative; no arbitrary code, comparisons, attributes or indexing.

inputs.name: integration_mesh
inputs.description: Feature-resolving finite increasing velocity mesh; infinite tails are also integrated.
inputs.constraints: All material features resolved; no unresolved tail features.

inputs.name: continuation
inputs.description: Add 2*pi*i*f(z) and derivative in the lower plane when true.

outputs.name: Z
outputs.description: Integral f(v)/(v-z) dv with the declared continuation.

supported: Safe AST algebra and analytic chain-rule derivative through DensityExpression.

excluded: Piecewise or nonanalytic expression syntax; use distribution selectors.
Automatic discovery of unresolved callback features.
preconditions: Density is real and integrable on the real contour.
No collective-mode uniqueness or certified global quadrature bound is asserted.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for invalid, nonfinite or singular declared inputs.

failure_semantics.nonconvergence: RuntimeError for Cauchy, real-axis or principal-value quadrature nonconvergence, or root nonconvergence.

scope: Safe AST algebra and analytic chain-rule derivative through DensityExpression.
Off-axis qualified Cauchy quadrature and real-axis subtracted principal value.
Centered and shifted Gaussian explicit-Hilbert derivatives at large phase, both half-planes and the real boundary; independent high-precision equations with componentwise zero absolute tolerance.
known_limitations: Real-axis local removable-point evaluation of the derivative integrand uses a symmetric second-derivative estimate; no global error certificate is returned.
Restricted parser supports finite real constants, pi, v, arithmetic, exp/log/sqrt/sin/cos/sinh/cosh/tanh.
Scientific validity is bounded by the tested numerical domain and applicability conditions.

example.description: Evaluate the analytic Lorentzian Hilbert/Cauchy transform on an explicit feature mesh.
example.code:
from scirel.kinetic.generalized_dispersion import evaluate_generalized_hilbert
z=.4-.7j
r=evaluate_generalized_hilbert(z,'1/(1+v**2)/pi',integration_mesh=[-20,-2,-1,0,1,2,20])
assert abs(r['Z']+1/(z+1j))<2e-9
example.expected: Observed PASS: the explicit integration mesh returns a finite transform matching -1/(z+i) within 2e-9.
